chronology: Recap: Honorata used Shabda-Oud time-acceleration on Okhar to survive, restore Oda, and build a planet-proof vessel; Honorata reincarnated inside Oda's restored body; Oda bore a son; Aghnar was decapitated but kept alive by machine and vowed to return and duel his son to the death.

Aghnar infiltrates the Imperial Palace at the center of the Galactic Confederacy, bypassing poly-radars, quantum sensors, and photonic barriers — mirroring a feat attributed to his father Othon von Salza.

Inside the palace, General Thato is publicly honored and awarded the first multicogan; permission is granted to distribute multicogans to the entire Purple Endoguard; the imperial assembly proclaims a universal-scale invasion under the divine empress Janus-Jana.
Aghnar's severed feet appear inside the supposedly impregnable palace, triggering panic, confusion, and calls to deploy the multicogan against the unknown intruder.
Aghnar destroys the Purple Endoguard as a demonstration of power, then publicly declares himself the new Metabaron and offers his services as a mercenary to the highest bidder in the imperial court.
A bidding war erupts among the Imperial House, the Techno-Pontificate, the Ekonomat, and the Confederacy of Colonial Planets for Aghnar's allegiance, lasting hours.
Aghnar's mercenary career: he assists the Gords in eliminating the fragrant aquatic Hireas on Planet Sec-Hum and suppresses a machine revolt on Nibal for the telepathic saurian Zerkots.
Aghnar leads the Troglosocialik armada against the aristocratic Cybergs in a space campaign, then allies with pirate Ulritch the Red to hijack an epiphyte cargo from three mother-coach ships.

Under contract to the Empress, Aghnar single-handedly destroys a 300,000-soldier battalion at Jupiter Nova in eight minutes; he also organizes relocation of the inhabitants of the depleted world Morga-the-Beautiful to the Teflon satellite.

Over roughly twenty years, Aghnar ages into an old man in his ruined hidden lair on sacred Anasirma, falling into a cycle of massacres, heavy drinking, and obsessive fixation on a tentacled being; he picks up a gun against himself.
Pthagurean ambassadors interrupt Aghnar's suicide attempt with a massive kublar payment offer; he lets them in.

Parallel war-council scenes: a bald leader nihilistically accepts a mercenary beast-faction's offer of total extermination across imperial planets; Mentreks are pressured to produce a strategic solution under threat of death.

Imperial officials execute Mentreks who suggest fleeing to the universe's edge; a surviving Mentrek warns that millions of Pthagurean ships led by the Metacraft are already in transit and will reach the empire's borders within twenty-four hours.
A cybernetic intellectual, threatened with disintegration, proposes the only remaining option: find a warrior stronger than the Metabaron and resolve the conflict through formal duel.

A noblewoman identifying herself as Oda and Honorata — widow of Othon von Salza and mother of Aghnar von Salza — enters the assembly wearing a holographic mask and claims her champion is already beside her; the disguise begins to drop.

Steelhead is publicly presented as a cyborg son of the current Metabaron and challenged to prove his worth; he creates the Golden Flower, a massive destructive energy construct, on command before the assembly.
Steelhead is formally appointed champion of the human galaxy; the Pythagoreans accept the challenge; a duel is scheduled for the following day.

A vast space battle erupts between millions of Pthagurean ships and millions of human ships; at its center, a black metacraft and a purple metacraft face each other in a father-versus-son duel between Aghnar and Steelhead — cliffhanger ending, continued in 'The Clash of the Meta-Warriors.'
locations: The Imperial Palace and Golden Planet (center of the Galactic Confederacy)
The forbidden zone surrounding the Imperial Palace
Anasirma (sacred mountain; site of Aghnar's ruined hidden lair)
Outer space battlefields (Troglosocialik-Cyberg campaign; Pthagurean-human fleet engagement)
lore_laws: The Shabda-Oud possess powers to accelerate time and a psycho-surgical science capable of restoring the dead to life.
A decapitated body can be kept alive indefinitely by attaching it to a machine.
Reincarnation or spirit-transfer into another living body is possible through Shabda-Oud methods.
The Metabaron title is successor-based and can be claimed by a combatant who supplants the current holder.
Metabaron tradition includes a formalized lethal duel between father and son as a recognized rite of succession.
The multicogan is a newly produced weapon presented as superior to all previously known arms.
The Golden Flower is a destructive construct of massive scale that can be created by the right individual on command.
A single Metabaron is sufficient to shift the military balance between otherwise evenly matched galaxies.
A formal duel between champions can be proposed and accepted as a legitimate mechanism to determine galactic-scale political outcomes.
Holographic masks can convincingly conceal a person's identity in public.
Intergalactic flight and resettlement are presented as feasible concepts within the setting.
Currency in the Galactic Confederacy is denominated in kublars.
major_events: Aghnar infiltrates the Imperial Palace and disrupts the Purple Endoguard mobilization ceremony, humiliating General Thato's security apparatus.
Aghnar destroys the Purple Endoguard, publicly claims the Metabaron title, and severs the Metabarons' hereditary service to the Imperial House to become a mercenary.
Aghnar conducts a decades-long mercenary career spanning multiple worlds and piracy before declining into isolated self-destruction at Anasirma.
Pthagurean ambassadors recruit Aghnar, interrupting his suicide attempt and drawing him into a galactic war.
The Mentreks propose a champion-duel solution and are executed for it; the surviving Mentrek's warning reveals the Pthagurean fleet is hours from the empire's borders.
Steelhead — cyborg son of Aghnar and Honorata-reincarnated-in-Oda — is publicly introduced and demonstrates his power by creating the Golden Flower before the assembly.
Steelhead is appointed champion of the human galaxy; a formal duel with his father Aghnar is arranged and the galaxy-scale battle begins.
open_uncertainties: The bio-mechanical head on the cover is not identified within the volume's pages.
The exact nature and identity of the tentacled being Aghnar is obsessively fixated on at Anasirma is not explained.
It is unclear whether both Mentreks are shot on p15 or only one is confirmed hit before the page ends.
The exact nature of the Golden Flower beyond its luminous destructive manifestation and the role of the red seed-like component in activating it are not fully explained.
The identity of the white-cloaked figure present when Aghnar destroys the Purple Endoguard is not stated.
Whether the Pthagureans recruited Aghnar to fight against the human empire or alongside it is ambiguous in these pages.
Printed page numbers in several pages do not match the provided page labels, suggesting a numbering discrepancy in the source scans.

The precise spelling of several faction and character names — including Troglosocialik, Cybergs, Hireas, Gords, Zerkots, and Ulritch the Red — depends on partially legible panel text and may be imperfect.
recurring_motifs: Father-son lethal challenge as Metabaron dynastic tradition
Bio-mechanical and cyborg integration of flesh and machinery
Mercenary loyalty overriding hereditary or moral obligation
Extreme violence as the primary proof of worth and succession
Money (kublars) as the only honest currency of allegiance
Lineage and bloodline determining political and cosmic destiny
Robot narrators framing the story with moral commentary and domestic interruption
Disguise and concealed identity (holographic masks, hidden lairs)
